terms.definition: A conceptual property a read model or aggregate exposes (what a consumer sees), NOT a column alias. A field carries a prose derivation and 0..N storage sources; it may be assembled through joins and sums or computed and never stored at all, so a field with sources:[] is correct, not incomplete. Fields sit on top of what the code reveals and never force a one-to-one field-to-column mapping.

anchors.symbol: A field is a conceptual property

terms.definition: The required prose sentence on every field saying HOW that field is produced (e.g. 'Sum of order_items.amount plus computed regional tax', or 'constant, hard-coded'). It is the human-readable lineage that stands even when there are zero machine-resolvable sources. In this tool's own self-model the stores are file-based / in-memory rather than SQL, so a derivation typically describes reading a JSON payload or an in-memory selector, not a column projection.

anchors.symbol: Every field carries a prose derivation

terms.definition: One entry in a field's sources[] array wiring the field to a physical column (or a raw dotted address) it draws from, tagged with a role and a transform. Zero sources is valid and common (computed / constant / unresolved). A source ref that looks like a local node id (col- tbl- db- srv-) MUST resolve to a known node or the merge errors; a free-form address string is accepted as-is.

The enum on a field source saying HOW that column relates to the field: 'derived-from' when it populates the field, 'filtered-by' / 'joined-on' / 'grouped-by' when it only influences the field, 'constant' for a fixed value. Nonstandard values merge as warnings, not errors.

The enum on a field source naming the OPERATION applied to the column on its way into the field: identity, transformation, aggregation, join, filter, lookup, or constant. It is orthogonal to role (role = why the column matters; transform = what is done to it). Nonstandard values merge as warnings.

Two independent per-field signals kept deliberately separate. 'conceptual' answers 'are we sure consumers see this field'; 'confidence' (high|medium|low) answers 'how sure are we of its derivation/sources'. A field can be conceptual and certain to exist yet still carry low source confidence, so the two must never be collapsed.

An append-only list on a field (and on physical nodes) recording HOW each piece of evidence was obtained: sql-literal, connection-string, orm-mapping, migration, inferred-from-dto, or assumed. Provenance appends, never overwrites, so a migration that corroborates a sql-literal finding raises confidence while the original code evidence stays. In this tool's own self-model, storage is recovered from file/in-memory reads rather than SQL, so its fields lean toward inferred-from-dto / assumed rather than sql-literal.

terms.term: Physical node types (server / database / table / column)
terms.definition: The four node types of the physical storage tier the behavioral model actually touches: server, database, table, and column (id prefixes srv- db- tbl- col-). Unlike behavioral stickies they default to inferred:false because the code literally names them, and they require a description but not an anchor. This is the vocabulary the tool RECOVERS FROM an analyzed codebase's SQL/ORM/config; the tool's OWN data layer is file-based/in-memory, so the self-model currently has no physical nodes.

How the physical tier nests: a column points to its table, a table to its database, a database to its server, via a 'parent' pointer rather than a flow edge. The merge enforces the level (column->table->database->server) and rejects cycles; a node parented at the wrong level is warned and dropped from the data-model tree. A node reached only through parent (or through a field source ref) still counts as referenced, so cited columns never orphan-warn.

terms.term: Data-model edge verbs (persists to / projects from / writes / connects via)
terms.definition: The four new behavioral-to-physical edge verbs: aggregate 'persists to' table, read model 'projects from' table, command 'writes' table, and any of command/readModel/aggregate 'connects via' server (existing 'reads' is reused for read access). They are demand-driven satellites attached by edges only; physical nodes are NEVER added to a flow's steps lane, exactly like invariants.

anchors.symbol: EDGE_VERBS (persists to / projects from / writes / connects via)

terms.definition: The stance that the data-model layer captures ONLY the servers/databases/tables/columns the behavioral model actually references, never a full-ERD dump. Only the columns a field references are added, never every column of a table. It keeps the layer strategic, the same spirit as 'prefer few, meaningful events', and answers 'what data does this read model/aggregate return and where does it come from' rather than describing the whole schema.

The traceable chain from a conceptual field back to the physical columns it draws from, expressed through derivation prose plus sources[] refs. The explorer can walk it in reverse (which fields draw from a given column) to answer impact questions before a schema change. Lineage is intentionally partial: a field with strong derivation prose and zero resolvable sources is a legitimate lineage endpoint, not a gap.

An optional pointer on an aggregate (and, in the data layer, on a database/server) saying its state actually lives INSIDE a named external system the tool does not deploy. The data-mapping phase reconciles with the existing ownedBy rather than inventing a parallel physical representation. In this self-model, agg-mcp-registration is ownedBy ext-claude-cli: the registration record lives in the Claude CLI's own config, not in a store this tool owns.
